$schema_notes: Machine-readable validation-case corpus (plan S3 deliverable). Each case is an operator report or a repo fixture *to be checked*, not a confirmed identification -- see docs/validation/corpus.md for the human-readable companion. Validated by tests/corpus/test_manifest.py.

cases.label_notes: Old catalog label '162.424' for this NOAA weather-radio group; frequency identity needs re-checking against the actual assignments.
cases.validation_question: Is speech present on NFM at these frequencies, and is msdr's tuning accurate against the true NOAA channel assignments?
cases.provenance: Operator report, not yet checked against an off-air recording.

cases.label_notes: North America APRS calling frequency; 1200 baud Bell 202 AFSK expected.
cases.validation_question: Tone/clock hypothesis (1200 Bd AFSK) vs a valid AX.25 FCS vs a fully parsed APRS payload -- which of the three does msdr actually reach on a live capture?
cases.provenance: Operator report, not yet checked against an off-air recording.

cases.label_notes: On/off keyed carrier activity reported; not assumed to be CW or any specific mode -- do not identify every keyed carrier as CW.
cases.validation_question: Is on/off keyed carrier activity present at this frequency, and if so what (if anything) can be said about its modulation?
cases.provenance: Operator report, not yet checked against an off-air recording.

cases.label_notes: 2 m repeater; old label '147.074' -- suspected frequency-mapping regression, needs re-verification.

cases.label_notes: Bursty land-mobile traffic; identity intentionally left open pending more dwells.

cases.label_notes: S4: the survey analyzer now classifies a synthetic GMSK 9600 burst as fm_fsk/9600 (family 'GMSK/FSK 9600 (AIS or packet)'), and msdr.decoder.pydecoders.ais.AisDecoder decodes a CRC-16/X.25-valid synthetic AIS frame end to end -- on synthetic fixtures only. This real 161.975/162.025 MHz capture is still not accessible, so field accuracy on it remains unproven; the allocation is a hint, never a decode.
cases.validation_question: Never identify AIS from frequency/allocation alone -- can msdr's IQ analyzer actually validate a GMSK/9600-baud hypothesis and produce integrity-checked (valid_frames > 0) AIS output?
cases.expected_outcome: GMSK/9600 hypothesis confirmed and validated (integrity=passed) frames produced on synthetic bursts -- tests/decoder/test_ais.py, tests/survey/test_families.py (GMSK -> fm_fsk 9600), tests/corpus/test_scorecard.py::test_ais_burst_decodes_or_is_honestly_unavailable. Field validation on a real 161.975/162.025 MHz capture is still pending (none accessible).
cases.provenance: Operator report; S4 closed the analyzer/decoder gap on synthetic fixtures (2026-09-27). Field capture still not accessible.

cases.label_notes: Operator-claimed station identities (KOIT 96.5, KLLC 97.3, KCRC 98.1, KSOL 98.9, KBRG 100.3, KRBQ 102.1, KBLX 102.9, KCPD 103.7, KNBR 104.5), reported mono/pilotless -- these are claims to verify, not ground truth. The two repo RDS fixtures (98.1/98.9) overlap this list; their decoded PI/PS/PTY are the evidence, the claimed callsigns are not corroborated by decode alone (RDS carries no station-name field; PS is an operator-settable label).
cases.validation_question: For each claimed station, does an off-air RDS/pilot-presence check support or contradict the operator's claimed identity, distinct from the frequency/allocation hint alone?
cases.provenance: Operator report of a 2026-09 FM-band listening session; 98.1/98.9 corroborated only insofar as rds-98100000-real-capture / rds-98900000-real-capture decode (see those cases).
